During a mayoral debate, Raman invoked the LAPD's 1979 Special Order 40 as a model of immigrant protection, describing the policy associated with the Daryl Gates era as a “gold standard.” She subsequently clarified that she was praising the policy, not Gates himself. articles.title: UAW Members Drive Ambitious Political Operation to Oust Commissioner Responsible for 8-Month Strike
articles.author: Justin Mayhugh
articles.content_excerpt: After months of organizing that began in the summer, the UAW is on track to knock the doors of tens of thousands of union members in Lorain County to turn out the vote against County Commissioner Jeff Riddell. Since February 18, UAW Local 2192 members from Lorain County Job and Family Services have been out on strike due to Commissioners like Riddell refusing to bargain in good faith and denying the $1 per hour raises the workforce needs to afford to survive today’s affordability crisis. Already the longest public-sector strike in Ohio’s history, the Lorain Country Job and Family Services strike is weeks from becoming the longest public-sector strike in U.S. history. articles.title: Where Did Black Los Angeles Go? The Disappearance of a Community That Built the City
articles.author: Sharon Kyle
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Part Two of Who Gets to Lead Los Angeles? Los Angeles celebrates its diversity. Its leaders routinely invoke the contributions of the many communities that have shaped the city. But something extraordinary has happened to one of those communities. Black Los Angeles has been disappearing. In 1980, approximately 496,000 Black people lived in Los Angeles, representing nearly 17 percent of its population. By 2020, that number had fallen to approximately 367,000, or about 9 percent. The city lost more than one-quarter of its Black population even as its overall population grew. articles.title: Minneapolis Refused to Take Trump’s Bait. It Paid Off.
articles.author: Eric Blanc
articles.content_excerpt: All signs point toward a resounding rebuke of Donald Trump in Tuesday’s midterm elections. Democrats have opened up a commanding lead in national polls , Trump’s popularity has sunk to historic lows, and even many of his former supporters are turning against him. There are plenty of reasons for this collapse, from rising prices to Trump’s disastrous war with Iran. But we shouldn’t forget what was arguably the single most important turning point of his presidency: the defeat of his militarized assault on Minneapolis. articles.author: Max B. Sawicky
articles.content_excerpt: It is common for mainstream news outlets and political commentators in the United States to describe socialists as “very liberal” or simply “progressive,” or to puzzle over how to draw ideological lines between democratic socialists and others on the broad Left. There are, in fact, serious differences — differences that socialists would do well to sharpen and articulate for the public. At the same time, as the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) grows by leaps and bounds, some commentators prefer to highlight those DSA positions that are furthest from common agreement. articles.author: Jo Blocton
articles.content_excerpt: Unions are the only space in American society where socialist values of solidarity and “us vs. them” are openly spoken and encouraged, outside of DSA. It is about time for us to take back this space to fight for workers’ rights. Detroit DSA’s Jobs Fair last month was as much about education as it was about encouraging folks to consider new job options. During the fair, about 60 participants heard from five different union members about why going to work in their fields can create legitimate change for the whole working class, while also improving their individual lives. The purpose was to bring socialists to the front line of the workforce, where we can build political power on all fronts for the working class. articles.title: Netanyahu Lost Israel's Election
articles.author: Jeffrey Sachs
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Benjamin Netanyahu , Itamar Ben-Gvir, and Bezalel Smotrich decisively lost Israel’s election on October 27. The governing coalition of Likud, the far right, and the ultra-Orthodox parties fell from 64 seats in 2022 to 53 , eight short of a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. The other 67 seats went to parties that campaigned to replace the government: 48 to the Jewish-led opposition headed by Gadi Eisenkot, a former army chief of staff, and 19 to the two Arab parties. Turnout was 77.9 percent, the highest since 1999, and Arab citizens, who make up about one-fifth of Israel’s population, voted at an estimated rate of about 80 percent , up from 53 percent in 2022 . articles.title: My Peace Shrine
articles.author: Pat Hynes
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Each morning, I walk to a peace shrine near me to contemplate what seems to be an unending cycle of wars and to pray for peace in the universal language of the heart shared among those who yearn for peace in our world. The shrine consists of a sturdy rusted iron circle enclosing a thin vertical metal rod and two shorter ones at acute angles to form a distinctive peace sign, placed atop a wooden support. It stands about five feet from the driveway’s edge near a small forest. Plants, such as jewelweed, a species of buckwheat with a distinct stem of pink flowers, and lamb’s quarters, are nearby companions. articles.title: A Palestinian Prisoner on the Nightmare Behind Israeli Bars
articles.author: Khalida Jarrar
articles.content_excerpt: Born in Nablus in 1963, Khalida Jarrar is one of the foremost voices of the Palestinian left — feminist, secular, socialist — and one of the towering figures of the political prisoners’ movement. For more than a decade she led Addameer, the main Palestinian prisoner support organization. In 2006, voters elected her to the Palestinian Legislative Council, where she chaired the prisoners’ commission, and she later served on the national committee that prepared Palestine’s accession to the International Criminal Court. Today she is a researcher at the Muwatin Institute at Birzeit University, where she is conducting a pioneering study of the class and gender dimensions of the women prisoners’ movement since 1967. articles.title: A Midterm Rout Will Hurt the GOP, but Trumpism Will Endure
articles.author: Joseph G. Peschek
articles.content_excerpt: Observers across the spectrum expect Democrats to make significant gains in the upcoming midterms, in House and Senate races and beyond. There are good reasons to trust in their predictions. Nonpresidential elections in the US are increasingly “nationalized,” meaning that evaluations of presidential and national politics strongly influence down-ballot choices. And President Donald Trump, having behaved cruelly and erratically while presiding over a weak economy and an unpopular war with Iran, has not set Republicans up for success. With inflation rates high, wages stagnant, and borrowing costs elevated, economic issues are central to the GOP’s current quandary. articles.title: In Italy, Giorgia Meloni Is Hardening Her Calls for Order
articles.author: Richard Braude
articles.content_excerpt: There’s a story doing the rounds. A woman is sitting in a bar in tourist-filled Turin; you can imagine the glass panes looking out onto the square, the little tables for spritzes and olives. Kids and chitchat. Then, out of nowhere, everyone starts coughing and wheezing; she feels a burning sensation in her eyes. The air is filled with white fumes, tear gas engulfing the little tables. Everyone rushes inside, they lock themselves in. Only afterward do they spy, through the fumes, a few hooded protesters running towards the piazza. Only afterward — when they can breathe more easily and slip into the side streets to make their way home — are the squares and streets fully taken over by skirmishes and barricades. articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. On November 3, 2026, Los Angeles voters will decide who leads their city. But on November 4, 2026 the rent will still be due. Homelessness, housing affordability, public safety, neighborhood services, and public trust will remain urgent concerns. The election will change the leadership question, not eliminate the challenges. The real test is not simply whether Karen Bass wins reelection or Nithya Raman becomes mayor. It is whether residents can turn their expectations into measurable commitments and ensure that whoever occupies City Hall answers to the people. articles.author: Tiqua Jackson
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. A non-relocating parent has legal rights that may allow them to challenge a child's proposed move, request a custody hearing, and seek changes to an existing parenting arrangement. When one parent plans to move to another city or state with the child, the other parent does not necessarily lose their say in the decision. Courts often evaluate relocation disputes using the best interests of the child standard , considering how the move could affect the child's well-being. A move-away lawyer can help the non-relocating parent understand their legal options and take appropriate steps to protect their parental rights. articles.title: CCTV Rules in Dubai
articles.author: Sejal Desai
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Security cameras are standard in Dubai shops, warehouses and offices, yet many employers overlook the legal side. A camera that records staff is collecting personal data, and that changes how it must be planned, explained and managed. This article covers the main rules on employee monitoring in the UAE, from camera placement to footage storage. The Legal Framework Behind Workplace Cameras Two sets of rules matter. Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data treats identifiable images of people as personal data, so recorded footage falls within its scope.
